summary: US-O1: A completed order can be refunded — the money returns and the journal records it
description:
**As** an organizer's support agent, **I want** to refund all or part of a completed order, **so that** a buyer who cannot attend gets their money back and the books still balance.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** — (first slice of the epic)

The money leg only. Commerce gains a staff-facing refund operation that resolves the order's captured payment, moves the money back through the existing PSP port (`/internal/psp/refund`, ADR-032), and appends a **compensating** fact to the hash-chained journal (ADR-003). Giving the capacity back and voiding the tickets is TKT-157 — a refund that returns money but leaves the seat sold is safe (it under-sells, never over-sells) and is the honest first tracer bullet.

**⚠️ Money path.** Anticipated and in scope for this ticket — the plan must state explicitly which existing money invariants it preserves.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Refunding q of Q tickets on a `completed` order returns exactly `q × unit_amount` through the PSP port. The amount is derived from the persisted `reservations.unit_amount`, **never** by dividing the order total — integer minor units throughout, no floats, no rounding step.
- [ ] The refund appends a **compensating** journal fact. The original sale fact is untouched (the journal's append-only trigger is the enforcement), and the payments chain still verifies after the refund.
- [ ] Idempotent under a stable idempotency key: a replay returns the same outcome and issues **exactly one** provider refund. A test proves two concurrent identical refund requests produce one `payment_compensations` row and one provider call.
- [ ] Cumulative refunded quantity can never exceed the order's quantity and cumulative refunded amount can never exceed what was captured. A test issues two partial refunds that would together over-refund and proves the second is refused.
- [ ] Refunding an order that is not `completed` is refused with a stated reason; refunding an already fully-refunded order is a replay (same answer), not an error.
- [ ] The post-refund order state distinguishes partial from full refund **and does not collide with the recovery state machine's existing `refunded` token** for compensated *failed* checkouts (ADR-016). Every existing switch over order status is checked, `classifyRecovered` included.
- [ ] The new operation is declared in commerce's `openapi.yaml` with every status it can answer (ADR-028), generated code is regenerated and committed, and the operation is exercised through the running stack in the smoke suite (ADR-030).

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001); regenerate and **commit** `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` before running the gate.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.

Traceability is a must, for money and tickets: money-relevant records land as immutable, hash-chained, signed journal entries from the first order (corrections = compensating entries; read models = projections), and every ticket/entitlement state change (issued, delivered, transferred, resold, exchanged, redeemed, reissued, invalidated) is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order.

governingAdrs.why: Corrections are COMPENSATING ENTRIES, never mutations. A refund/exchange appends a new signed fact; the original sale fact and its hash link are untouched. The payments journal has a DB trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE — any design that 'adjusts' a fact is rejected by the database, not by review.

All provider money movement goes through the PSP port. `/internal/psp/refund` and the `payment_compensations` table already exist (TKT-114/116) — the PRIMARY KEY (organizer, source_idempotency_key, kind) is what converges duplicate refunds onto ONE provider idempotency key. Reuse it; do not add a parallel refund path.

The checkout journal protocol defines how commerce records money facts (order_facts row → payments /internal/facts, deterministic fact_id, idempotent). A post-purchase money movement uses the same protocol; do not invent a second one.

TRAP: the orders status vocabulary ALREADY contains `refunded`, and the recovery runner writes it for a COMPENSATED FAILED CHECKOUT (money taken for an order that never completed). A post-purchase refund of a COMPLETED order is a different thing. Reusing the token would make recovery's classifyRecovered() treat a refunded completed order as a terminal checkout failure. Pick distinct tokens and check every switch over order status.

Fail closed. Responses are validated against the spec; an undeclared status code becomes a 500. Every new endpoint must declare every status it can answer, and a downstream answer commerce cannot validate aborts rather than degrades.

Contract-first. A new operation is written in the service's openapi.yaml first, then `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and COMMITTED before the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Commerce and inventory ARE inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate. A new documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.

Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job. Add the SQL under the service's internal/store/migrations/ with the next number; the server path never migrates.

objective.note: The epic's whole post-purchase story stands on one primitive: money can come back and the trail still proves it. Everything else in TKT-9 (partial, exchange, bulk cancellation) is a caller of this.

scope.note: IN: commerce refund operation, PSP refund via the existing port, compensating journal fact, order/reservation refund state, idempotency and over-refund guards. OUT: inventory capacity return and ticket voiding (TKT-157), exchange (TKT-158), bulk cancellation (TKT-159), fees/taxes on refunds (TKT-6/TKT-32), buyer-facing self-service refunds (TKT-21/TKT-22), refund-protection add-on (TKT-8).

uncertainties.note: The exact status tokens for a partially/fully refunded completed order are a Planning-time call — constrained by ADR-016's existing `refunded`, reversible within one migration. Whether the refund is a new table or columns on `orders` is likewise Planning's.

dependencies.note: No blockers. The PSP refund port, `payment_compensations`, the journal and the completed-order path all exist on main today (TKT-114/116, TKT-153).

approach.note: New commerce operation → resolve the order's captured payment operation → payments `/internal/psp/refund` under a deterministic key → compensating fact through the existing `s.fact` protocol → guarded status write. Test seam: commerce's api server_test plus the payments journal chain verification already in the gate.

first_slice.note: A full refund of a single-line completed order, proven end to end; partial quantity is the same code path with q < Q and is in the same slice because the guard maths only exists once.

success.note: Demoable through the running stack: complete an order, refund it, show the provider refund, the compensating fact, and a still-verifying chain.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition; 8 governing ADRs with per-ticket constraints, including the ADR-016 status-token trap.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-156 (US-O1)

**Selection reason.** First child of TKT-9 and the only one of the four with **zero blockers** —
TKT-157/158/159 are all blocked-by it, directly or transitively, so it has maximum unblocking power
and there is nothing else to choose between.

**Blocker check:** `links` carries `blocks TKT-157` and no `blocked-by`. Zero open blockers.

**Branch:** `TKT-156-order-refund-money` off `origin/main` @ `0911713`.

**Gate waiver.** This ticket runs under the **gateless waiver recorded on the epic (TKT-9,
`kind=claim`)**: all four human gates are waived by the repo owner as a process experiment. Gate 2
is self-resolved from the cross-model critique, Gate 3 is an agent squash-merge after the ai-review
converges, Gate 4 is a self-validation against test evidence on the merged code. Model routing, TDD,
cross-model review and the local gate are unchanged.

**Mémo revalidation at claim (the mémo is a shaping-time snapshot).** Re-resolved
`governingAdrs` against `docs/adr/` at HEAD `0911713`: all eight named ADRs exist and none has been
superseded since the 2026-07-31 bake — the bake and the claim are the same day, so no drift is
possible. Highest ADR on main is **ADR-036**; the mémo's list is current.

**Risk:** not `risk:low`. This is a money path across two services with a new persisted state.

**Models for this ticket** (`.claude/sdlc.config.json`, unmodified): plan = `gpt-5.6-sol` (Codex),
planReview = `main-agent` (this session, Claude Opus 5), implement = `main-agent`,
aiReview = `gpt-5.6-sol` (Codex). Both cross-model pairs hold: plan ≠ planReview, implement ≠
aiReview.
